subject.title: feat(whatsapp): agent tools for group create / add participants / invite link

question: What authorization boundary should WhatsApp group create, add-participants, and invite-link tools require before they can call the linked listener?
rationale: These tools mutate or expose access to third-party chats through a linked WhatsApp identity, and the generic ChannelAgentTool execute contract does not currently provide sender context by itself.

options.title: Require operation-specific authorization
options.body: Add maintainer-approved owner, sender, or tool-policy checks before listener calls and keep the global groups flag as only the coarse opt-in.

options.title: Accept the global groups gate
options.body: Treat channels.whatsapp.actions.groups as the complete security boundary, accepting that any agent with the tool can perform these group-admin operations once enabled.

options.title: Pause behind authorization work
options.body: Keep this PR paused until the adjacent WhatsApp sender-authorization work defines a reusable policy surface for group-admin tools.

recommendation.title: Require operation-specific authorization
recommendation.body: Add maintainer-approved owner, sender, or tool-policy checks before listener calls and keep the global groups flag as only the coarse opt-in.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is primarily about plugin/security boundary shape rather than the Baileys socket call itself, matching recent plugin-boundary history.
